artists.biography:
All About Eve were a British rock/pop band. The creative core consisted of the Coventry born Julianne Regan (vocals), and the Huddersfield born Andy Cousin (bass guitar), with other members changing over the years. Their biggest commercial success was "Martha's Harbour" (1988), although the band's tenure ran between 1984 and 2004, and included four UK Top 50 albums.

Julianne Regan, a former journalist, played bass in an early line-up of the gothic rock group Gene Loves Jezebel. before leaving to join All About Eve, previously known as the Swarm. The initial core of All About Eve was Regan, guitarist Tim Bricheno, and bassist Andy Cousin. As a three-piece (plus a drum machine), they released a series of independent singles in the mid 1980s including "D for Desire", "In the Clouds" and "Flowers In Our Hair". After Regan sang backing vocals for The Mission's God's Own Medicine album, the band received greater attention and were signed to Phonogram. Drummer Mark Price was added around this time.

perplexity.description:
All About Eve, released in 1988 on Mercury/Phonogram, is the debut studio album by the British rock band All About Eve. Musically, the album blends ethereal gothic rock with dreamy pop sensibilities, drawing comparisons to bands like Cocteau Twins and Siouxsie and the Banshees. The sound is characterized by lush guitar textures, atmospheric production, and Julianne Regan’s distinctive vocals, with lyrics often inspired by hippie ideals, white magic, and fairy tale imagery. Produced primarily by Paul Samwell-Smith, the album features a mix of acoustic and electric instrumentation, creating a unique blend of melancholy and optimism.

The album stands as a cornerstone in All About Eve’s discography, marking their breakthrough and establishing their signature style. It was their most commercially successful release, reaching No. 7 on the UK Albums Chart and spending 29 weeks in the top 100. Certified Gold for sales exceeding 100,000 copies, it spawned four Top 40 singles, including the Top 10 hit “Martha’s Harbour.” Critics praised its atmospheric production and emotional depth, solidifying its reputation as a defining album of the late-1980s British rock scene.
